However, the data had limited statistical power and the review was unable to exclude the possibility that indometacin may increase the risk of adverse neonatal outcomes. The ev- idence for efficacy of cyclo-oxygenase inhibitors is based on small studies,34 and because of the potential for adverse effects, indometacin is generally reserved as a second-line drug or given with other tocolytics for an additive effect.12 More recently it has been suggested that the enzyme isoform cyclo-oxygenase-2 is associat- ed with labour, while cyclo-oxygenase-1 is responsible for constant prostaglandin synthesis in body tissues. The role of cyclo-oxygenase-2 inhibitors in the treatment or prevention of premature labour remains investigational. • Other drugs are under investigation. Application of patches of the nitric oxide donor glyceryl trinitrate to the abdomen to produce uterine relaxation was reported to be as effective as ritodrine treatment.35 However, anoth- er study36 found transdermal glyceryl trinitrate to be less effective than beta agonists, and a systematic review37 concluded that there was insufficient evidence to sup- port its routine use. When acute tocolysis has successfully suppressed uterine activity, the use of maintenance therapy has been tried to prevent recurrent episodes of premature labour. However, a systematic review38 found that although there was a small but significant increase in the number of days gained before delivery, maintenance therapy did not reduce the in- cidence of premature birth or recurrent premature labour; there was also a non-significant trend towards an increase in adverse perinatal outcomes.
